I had to disable the extension because all my components were having this warning and was really annoying.
In my case the problem was with the IonicModule. Angular couldn't detect al `<ion-xxxx>` items even though I had the IonicModule imported in all modules and submodules.

Same problem here, but with Angular Material, my own components, async pipe and many more. The app compiles just fine, but the LS is like screaming at me that everything is not a known element. Pretty annoying.
I'm using a nx workspace, created two weeks ago and this issue exists since then. My workaround was disabling the Ivy mode, hoping with v12 it gets resolved, but today I upgraded my workspace to angular v12 and the problem still persists.

In my other workspace I have kinda the same problems, but the usually resolve after restating the LS, at least for a while.
Any ideas on that?

Same problem on Linux/Mint.
Fixed it temporary by downgrading VSCode to v1.55.2.

@naturalfreak the specific issue for the language service and the project you linked is the re-export of the module. If you were to change that to an inline export (`export class DrawerModule`), everything works correctly. I have to sync with our compiler expert tomorrow to investigate why this diagnostic only surfaces in the language service. 

@ekzGuille @arndwestermann @zeljkoantich - Are you able to provide an example project where this can be reproduced? Without that, there's not much more investigation we can do here other than looking at the [somewhat limited] information that's provided by the server logs.

rename.to: Modules not exported inline (export class MyModule) are not recognized by language service

body:
This particular error happens because we configured the compiler for the language service to skip modules that aren't exported. This was done because the program used for the language service generally includes a much larger set of files than what is used to compile the application. That is, `tsconfig`s often include the `*spec` files as well. The result is that modules defined in tests could cause errors for various reasons (for example, a component is declared in the application module as well as the test module). 
To get around this, we skip non-exported modules, assuming those would be test modules. Our check for that needs to be more robust so that it does not skip modules which are exported later on in the file as in `export {DrawerModule}`. 
I should be able to get a fix out for this today.

@arndwestermann your issue doesn't seem related to this. If you can figure out a way to reproduce the error and share a project that we can use to debug, please provide that information in https://github.com/angular/vscode-ng-language-service/issues/1353
Transferring this to angular/angular as this is fundamentally a compiler bug (we need to be smarter about detecting "exported" components).
